title: Brother George: playing by ear, Jimmy Ryan's and the Esquire award
summary: Mrs. Brunies and Brunies tell stories of brother George playing in the dark, his wedding parade at Jimmy Ryan's and the Esquire award.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I read an editorial one time about George. When he was up north, and the lights went out or something happened, the electricity, I don't know what. And he was the only man who could play because he was playing by ear. He was the only one who could play, all the rest of them. Had no lights, but he kept playing. You know, the comic book.

Did George ever tell you about the time when he was married at Jimmy Ryan's in New York in 52nd? I remember. He wasn't doing any business. He had just started the place, you see. So he takes the band out of the place. All along with the 2nd Street, playing a dog time strutters ball. He's playing the jail.
Hit the front pages of the Daily Noon. They still do that sometimes.
He was the All-American trombone listener.
Well, I'm sorry. I can't have that book. It's a dial-up. It was Esquire, wasn't it?
Esquire. Oh, the Esquire book. That's right. I remember. I've seen that.
Some years back. And he was the All-American. He claimed to be the All-American trombone listener.
